build.prompt_version: Trump Diary — Weekly Thread Package Prompt v1

week.headline: The eighth week of Trump’s second term did not hinge on a single shock.
week.summary: The eighth week of Trump’s second term did not hinge on a single shock. It unfolded instead as a dense layering of decisions that altered who counts, who serves, and who remembers. Immigration rules, civil service structures, university budgets, and media funding all shifted in ways that looked technical when taken alone. Together, they traced a sharper outline of a state that answers more to personal power and aligned wealth than to law, expertise, or equal citizenship.

evidence_items.title: Civil service structures shifted this week
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The week summary explicitly identifies civil service structures as one of the main arenas of change, signaling that bureaucratic control and institutional remaking are central to the week's narrative.

evidence_items.title: Technical-looking decisions accumulate into a state answering to personal power
evidence_items.why_it_matters: This language maps directly onto administrative capture: state machinery is being reoriented away from neutral expertise and toward personalist control through cumulative institutional decisions.

evidence_items.title: Agency and governance changes treated as part of a layered restructuring week
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The digest is identified as a core source for the week, and the week summary indicates that multiple bureaucratic domains were altered together rather than as isolated incidents.

thread_states.summary: Administrative capture remains one of the clearest explanatory frames for Week 8. The week is described not as a single rupture but as an accumulation of seemingly technical changes that restructure who serves and how institutions operate, with civil-service change functioning as a core mechanism of personalized governance.
continuity_notes: This appears to carry directly forward from prior weeks rather than debut here.
Week 8 deepens the pattern by making administrative restructuring feel routine and technical rather than spectacular.
The rewrite should connect agency and staffing change to the broader erosion of neutral state capacity.

evidence_items.title: Prior-week continuity context

The week's institutional changes imply continuing concentration of authority even without a single headline-grabbing emergency or direct separation-of-powers clash.

Week 8 points to a governance environment in which law is increasingly subordinated to power, but the strongest evidence here sits in institutional restructuring rather than explicit justice-system episodes.

evidence_items.title: Immigration developments embedded in a larger hierarchy-of-belonging week

Connect immigration developments to university pressure and rights hierarchy where appropriate, but keep immigration machinery itself visible.

thread_states.canonical_name: Information control, record erasure, and public-memory manipulation

evidence_items.title: Media funding shifted this week
evidence_items.why_it_matters: Changes to media funding fit this thread directly because they affect the public information environment and the independence of knowledge-distributing institutions.

evidence_items.title: The week altered who remembers
evidence_items.why_it_matters: That phrase points directly to memory politics and the shaping of public knowledge, not merely to ordinary communications strategy.

evidence_items.title: State answers less to law and expertise
evidence_items.why_it_matters: Information control often works by downgrading expertise, records, and institutional knowledge; the week summary makes that erosion of expert authority explicit.

thread_states.summary: Information control is a lead frame for Week 8 because the week is explicitly about memory, expertise, and the funding and shaping of public knowledge institutions. Media funding changes and the summary's emphasis on 'who remembers' make this more than background narrative management.
continuity_notes: This continues prior weeks' pressure on information channels, but here it appears in a more institutional and budgetary form.
The rewrite should stress that information control is being operationalized through funding and institutional leverage, not just rhetoric.
Link media funding to broader knowledge-system pressure, including universities where useful.

evidence_items.title: Week traced a state answering more to aligned wealth

evidence_items.title: Technical policy shifts linked to power and wealth rather than neutral governance

thread_states.summary: Crony capitalism is not the dominant storyline, but Week 8 explicitly ties state action to aligned wealth. That makes this thread more than background and suggests a renewed visibility of insider-serving governance within the week's broader institutional restructuring.
continuity_notes: Marking as reborn reflects a week in which private-state fusion becomes textually explicit again after not being the clearest foreground frame every recent week.
Use this thread to sharpen the motive structure behind technical state changes.
Do not overtake the more operational lead threads with enrichment language unless week details strongly support it.

Use it to connect immigration, campus pressure, and institutional restructuring into one larger rights-order story.

This gives the week a concrete institutional arena in which federal leverage disciplines semi-independent bodies that can host expertise, dissent, and alternative memory.
continuity_notes: Marking as reborn reflects a sharper standalone visibility this week, even if related pressure existed earlier.
This thread should be used to connect university pressure to both information control and stratified rights.

week_summary_notes: Week 8 is best understood as a cumulative institutional week rather than a single-crisis week.
The strongest narrative collision is between administrative capture, immigration-based hierarchy, information control, and rights stratification.
University and media funding changes make civil-society and knowledge-institution pressure more central than in some adjacent weeks.
Crony-capitalist motive is present but should remain subordinate to the operational story of state restructuring.
Several later-year coercion threads, especially domestic militarization and anti-dissent suppression, should not be imported too aggressively into this earlier week.

rewrite_guidance.opening_focus: Open on the week's cumulative character: a cluster of technical-looking changes across immigration, civil service, universities, and media that together reveal a sharper state hierarchy about who belongs, who serves, and what institutions are allowed to know or remember.
rewrite_guidance.closing_focus: Close by stressing that the week's significance lies in consolidation rather than spectacle: the machinery of governance is being quietly reoriented toward personal power, aligned wealth, weakened expertise, and unequal citizenship.
continuity_emphasis_notes: Emphasize that administrative restructuring is not isolated policy churn but a continuing method of governing.
Tie immigration developments to a broader hierarchy of belonging rather than treating them as a separate silo.
Show university and media funding pressure as linked efforts to discipline knowledge institutions and civil society.
Use rights-stratification language to connect otherwise disparate policy domains.
If mentioning crony capitalism, frame it as motive and beneficiary structure behind the week's institutional moves, not as the sole storyline.
